role: forecasting and control (world-model prediction / rollout), NOT anomaly detection

selected_forecaster.name: WorldModelV2 / feat_h12_w24
selected_forecaster.spec: action-conditioned ridge + per-horizon LightGBM residuals (200 trees, 63 leaves, lr 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.8, min_child_samples 100); history 12; engineered per-sensor rolling mean/std/rate over a 24-step window (offsets clamped at the segment start). Horizons 1 and 5; seed 0.
selected_forecaster.supersedes_for_forecasting: the rt1/rt2 selected forecaster (ridge + 60-tree GBR, history 3), which remains the SELECTED DETECTOR world model and is NOT replaced for detection

why: On held-out NORMAL HAI validation the v2 forecaster reduces multi-step forecast error over the rt1/rt2 baseline: exploration measured H5 MAE -12% and H1 -4.5% (docs/research/real_telemetry_world_model_exploration_v1.json); an independent retrospective on all three real HAI releases confirmed a consistent normal-period forecast-MAE gain (H5 +1.8% / +1.9% / +3.6%) on the recorded data (docs/research/real_telemetry_detection_v2_retrospective.json). Two independent levers compound: history length (plateau ~12) and rolling summary features over a window longer than the history (plateau ~24).
scope_and_caveats: This selection is for FORECASTING / CONTROL use only. The same retrospective showed the v2 forecaster does NOT improve residual-based attack DETECTION (it predicts through anomalies, shrinking the residual spike), so the detector keeps the rt1/rt2 history-3 world model. Detection improvement is a separate, open question pursued under docs/research/real_telemetry_detection_protocol_v2.json (awaiting fresh attack data).
The registered rt1/rt2 frozen bundles and the incident-dynamics models are NOT retrained or altered by this selection.
Absolute forecast-MAE numbers carry mild selection optimism (model chosen on the same validation family); the relative ranking is robust across fit sizes and all three releases.
